simple.meaning: סְגַן (çᵉgan) is a Hebrew word meaning “governor.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: סְגַן (H5460) appears 5 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Daniel 2:48, with occurrences in Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to סְגַן (H5460) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in סְגַן (H5460) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: סְגַן (çᵉgan) / H5460 is traced through Daniel 2:48, Daniel 3:2, Daniel 3:3, Daniel 3:27 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Then the king made Daniel great, and gave him many great gifts, and made him rule over the whole province of Babylon, and to be chief governor over all the wise men of Babylon.

timeline.evidenceText: Then the king made Daniel great, and gave him many great gifts, and made him rule over the whole province of Babylon, and to be chief governor over all the wise men of Babylon.

Then Nebuchadnezzar the king sent to gather together the local governors, the deputies, and the governors, the judges, the treasurers, the counselors, the sheriffs, and all the rulers of the provinces, to come to the dedication of the image which Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up.

Then the local governors, the deputies, and the governors, the judges, the treasurers, the counselors, the sheriffs, and all the rulers of the provinces, were gathered together to the dedication of the image that Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up; and they stood before the image that Nebuchadnezzar had set up.

The local governors, the deputies, and the governors, and the king’s counselors, being gathered together, saw these men, that the fire had no power on their bodies. The hair of their head wasn’t singed. Their pants weren’t changed, the smell of fire wasn’t even on them.
Now, O king, establish the decree, and sign the writing, that it not be changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which doesn’t alter.”
